Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Inbound exploitation of Cisco Unified CM WebDialer SSRF (CVE-2026-20230) from campaign infra · [LLM] Cisco Unified CM SSRF file:// arbitrary file-write payload (CVE-2026-20230)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Rogue Apache Axis AdminService / JSP webshell on Cisco Unified CM (CVE-2026-20230 post-exploit)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains

Inbound exploitation of Cisco Unified CM WebDialer SSRF (CVE-2026-20230) from campaign infra AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to the Cisco Unified CM WebDialer service that carry SSRF exploit markers (file://, Apache Axis AdminService) or originate from the Defused-reported campaign IP 156.146.38.167. This is the initial-access step Cisco confirmed is under active exploitation. Rationale: Anchored on the corroborated exploit chain (WebDialer service + Apache Axis AdminService + file:// SSRF) confirmed by Cisco's advisory, SOCRadar and DarkReading; the campaign IP 156.146.38.167 is currently single-source (Defused) so it is used as a booster, not the sole anchor. Defender/Falcon left empty because CUCM is a Linux Tomcat appliance not onboarded to EDR — detection lives on the wire (CEF) and in appliance syslog. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-cucm-ssrf-cXPnHcW • https://socradar.io/blog/cve-2026-20230-cisco-unified-cm-webdialer-ssrf/ • https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/less-than-24-hours-attackers-weaponize-cisco-cucm-flaw
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WebDialer click-to-call SOAP traffic from internal CTI/UC applications (will lack file:// and AdminService markers)
  • Authorized vulnerability scanners (Tenable/Qualys/Rapid7) probing the WebDialer endpoint from a known scan subnet
  • Internal penetration-test or Cisco TAC-guided validation of the patch from a corporate source IP
  • Security-team replaying the public PoC from a sanctioned research host
Suppression filter
| where not (RequestURL has "webdialer" and not (RequestURL has_any ("file://","file:/","AdminService","/axis/")) and SourceIP !in (CampaignIPs))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the destination is a Unified CM host and inspect the full RequestURL for a file:// scheme or Axis AdminService call; check whether WebDialer is enabled and whether the CUCM version predates 14SU6/15SU5. 2) Contain: block SourceIP 156.146.38.167 at the perimeter, disable the WebDialer service (Cisco's interim mitigation), and restrict WebDialer to trusted management networks. 3) Hunt: pivot to the same DestinationIP for follow-on /axis/ AdminService requests and newly created .jsp files under the Tomcat web root (see webshell UC), and review CUCM install/security logs for unexpected files.
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["156.146.38.167"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RequestURL has "webdialer"
| where SourceIP in (CampaignIPs)
   or RequestURL has_any ("file://", "file:/", "AdminService", "/axis/", "%2Ffile", "%66%69%6c%65")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction, RequestClientApplication
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Cisco Unified CM SSRF file:// arbitrary file-write payload (CVE-2026-20230) AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP requests to a Unified CM host whose URI/query embeds a file:// scheme, the mechanism Defused observed attackers using to write attacker-controlled files onto the appliance via the WebDialer SSRF. Content-pivot detection independent of source IP. Rationale: Uses the article's specific technique string 'properly constructed file:// payloads to create files' plus the corroborated Axis/WebDialer target paths; matches on request content so it fires regardless of rotating source IPs. URL-encoded variants included because SSRF payloads are commonly percent-encoded to bypass filters. Cross-checked against: • https://socradar.io/blog/cve-2026-20230-cisco-unified-cm-webdialer-ssrf/ • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-cucm-ssrf-cXPnHcW
ATT&CKT1190 T1105
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security scanners injecting file:// test strings during authorized SSRF assessments
  • WAF/IPS logging the raw payload of a blocked request (verify DeviceAction shows block, not allow)
  • Developers or Cisco TAC reproducing the PoC in a lab that shares the SIEM
  • Legitimate application passing a file: parameter unrelated to CUCM (excluded by the webdialer/axis/ccmadmin path requirement)
Suppression filter
| where DeviceAction !in~ ("blocked","denied","drop","reset")
Response runbook
1) Triage: decode the file:// path in RequestURL to see what the attacker attempted to read/write, and confirm whether the WAF allowed or blocked (DeviceAction). 2) Contain: if allowed, isolate the CUCM host from untrusted networks, disable WebDialer, and snapshot the appliance for forensics before patching to 14SU6/15SU5. 3) Hunt: search the same host for follow-on /axis/services/AdminService calls and newly written .jsp files, and review CUCM audit logs for unexpected OS-level files created around the request timestamp.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RequestURL has_any ("webdialer", "/axis/", "/ccmadmin/")
| where RequestURL has_any ("file://", "file:%2F%2F", "file:/", "%66%69%6c%65%3a")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Rogue Apache Axis AdminService / JSP webshell on Cisco Unified CM (CVE-2026-20230 post-exploit) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the post-SSRF stage where attackers invoke the Apache Axis AdminService on the CUCM Tomcat stack to deploy a rogue SOAP service and then access an attacker-dropped .jsp webshell in the web root — the code-execution/persistence tail of the CVE-2026-20230 chain. Rationale: Targets the corroborated post-exploit chain (SOCRadar/DarkReading: rogue Apache Axis service deployed via AdminService, then a JSP file-writer/command shell in the Tomcat web dir). AdminService invocation and new .jsp access on a production CUCM are highly abnormal, giving a sharp signal distinct from the initial SSRF request. Cross-checked against: • https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/less-than-24-hours-attackers-weaponize-cisco-cucm-flaw • https://socradar.io/blog/cve-2026-20230-cisco-unified-cm-webdialer-ssrf/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cisco built-in .jsp application pages accessed during normal CCMAdmin/Self-Care usage (baseline the specific known .jsp set)
  • Cisco upgrade/COP file installation touching Tomcat webapps
  • Authorized admin using legitimate Axis-based CUCM management functions from a management host
  • Vulnerability scanner fingerprinting the /axis/ path
Suppression filter
| where not (RequestURL contains ".jsp" and DestinationHostName !has "cucm" and RequestURL !has "AdminService")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the exact .jsp path and whether it exists in a stock CUCM image; a non-catalog .jsp or any external-sourced GET/POST to /axis/services/AdminService is high-confidence malicious. 2) Contain: isolate the CUCM host, capture the .jsp and Tomcat logs, and treat the appliance as root-compromised — plan rebuild/restore rather than in-place cleanup. 3) Hunt: correlate back to the originating SSRF file:// request and source IP, review outbound connections from the CUCM host for C2/reverse shell, and check for credential/config exfiltration and lateral movement from the appliance.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RequestURL has_any ("/axis/services/AdminService", "AdminService", "/axis/services")
   or (RequestURL contains ".jsp" and RequestURL has_any ("/webdialer/", "/axis/", "/ccmadmin/", "/cucm-uds/"))
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20230")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20230")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CISA: Microsoft SharePoint RCE flaw now actively exploited

BleepingComputer
2026-07-02 6 use cases 2 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

CISA warned on Wednesday that attackers have begun exploiting a high-severity Microsoft SharePoint remote code execution vulnerability patched in May. [...]

CVEsCVE-2026-45659
ATT&CKT1190 T1486
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] SharePoint IIS worker (w3wp.exe) spawns shell/LOLBIN — CVE-2026-45659 deserialization RCE
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SharePoint worker (w3wp.exe) writes .aspx web shell into LAYOUTS web root — CVE-2026-45659 post-exploit
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
SharePoint IIS worker (w3wp.exe) spawns shell/LOLBIN — CVE-2026-45659 deserialization RCE AIExploitation High
Hunts the code-execution step of the CVE-2026-45659 SharePoint deserialization RCE: the gadget chain runs in the context of the SharePoint application-pool worker (w3wp.exe), which then spawns a command interpreter or LOLBIN. A production SharePoint server's IIS worker process essentially never spawns cmd/powershell/certutil, so this is high-fidelity for exploitation. Rationale: Grounded in the article's core claim that CVE-2026-45659 lets an authenticated attacker 'execute code remotely on the SharePoint Server' via deserialization; corroborating write-ups (Akamai, Trellix, Rapid7) confirm the payload runs as the w3wp.exe app-pool identity, and w3wp spawning cmd/powershell is the canonical exploitation signal for SharePoint deserialization RCE. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/microsoft-patches-sharepoint-rce-flaw.html • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/26/sharepoint-vulnerability-cve-2026-45659/ • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/sharepoint-vulnerability-rce-active-exploitation-detections-mitigations • https://www.trellix.com/blogs/research/toolshell-unleashed-decoding-the-sharepoint-attack-chain/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-zero-day-exploitation-of-microsoft-sharepoint-servers-cve-2025-53770/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate SharePoint timer/health scripts or admin PSConfig runs that spawn cmd/powershell under the STS/app-pool context during patching
  • Monitoring agents (SCOM, custom probes) invoking net.exe or whoami.exe under the IIS worker for health checks
  • Backup or DLP integrations that shell out from a custom SharePoint web part
  • Non-SharePoint IIS sites sharing a w3wp.exe binary name where a web app legitimately shells out
  • Post-patch validation tooling that queries app-pool identity via whoami
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("psconfig", "Microsoft.SharePoint.Administration") and InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the host is a SharePoint server and pull the full child command line + SHA256; look for encoded/download strings, machine-key/web.config reads, or recon (whoami/net). Check whether the CVE-2026-45659 May 2026 update (SharePoint 2016/2019/Subscription Edition) is installed. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the server from the network, kill the offending process tree, and preserve w3wp memory/IIS logs; if compromise confirmed, rotate the SharePoint MachineKey/ASP.NET keys (stolen keys enable forged-request persistence). 3) HUNT: Pivot to UC2 (web-shell writes into LAYOUTS), review IIS logs for the originating authenticated account and source IP, and sweep other internet-exposed SharePoint servers for the same w3wp child-spawn pattern.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\curl.exe","\\net.exe","\\net1.exe","\\whoami.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SharePoint w3wp.exe Spawning Shell or LOLBIN (CVE-2026-45659 Deserialization RCE)
id: 8f2b1c4d-6a7e-4b3f-9c21-5d8e0a1f7b62
status: experimental
description: Detects the SharePoint IIS application-pool worker (w3wp.exe) spawning a command interpreter or LOLBIN, the code-execution step of the CVE-2026-45659 deserialization RCE.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-microsoft-sharepoint-rce-flaw-now-actively-exploited/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/microsoft-patches-sharepoint-rce-flaw.html
  - https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/sharepoint-vulnerability-rce-active-exploitation-detections-mitigations
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/02
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\CertUtil.exe OR *\\net.exe OR *\\whoami.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/w3wp\.exe/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|mshta|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|net|net1|whoami)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
SharePoint worker (w3wp.exe) writes .aspx web shell into LAYOUTS web root — CVE-2026-45659 post-exploit AIInstallation High
Hunts the persistence step after CVE-2026-45659 exploitation: the SharePoint IIS worker process writing a new web-accessible handler (.aspx/.ashx/.asmx) into the SharePoint LAYOUTS/Web Server Extensions directory. Legitimate SharePoint provisions these files via the installer/solution deployment, not from the live w3wp worker at runtime — so a runtime write here is a strong web-shell indicator. Rationale: The article states CVE-2026-45659 grants RCE with the SharePoint process's permissions; corroborating SharePoint-RCE research (Akamai, Trellix, Rapid7) shows attackers immediately drop .aspx web shells into the LAYOUTS web root (C:\Program Files\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\Web Server Extensions\..\TEMPLATE\LAYOUTS\), and a runtime write of a new handler by w3wp.exe is not legitimate SharePoint behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/sharepoint-vulnerability-rce-active-exploitation-detections-mitigations • https://www.trellix.com/blogs/research/toolshell-unleashed-decoding-the-sharepoint-attack-chain/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-zero-day-exploitation-of-microsoft-sharepoint-servers-cve-2025-53770/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/microsoft-patches-sharepoint-rce-flaw.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SharePoint cumulative-update / PSConfig deployment writing provisioned .aspx pages into LAYOUTS during patching windows
  • WSP solution package deployment (Add-SPSolution/Install-SPSolution) staging application pages
  • Third-party SharePoint add-ins provisioning custom application pages at first activation
  • Admin manual copy of a legitimate application page authored under the app-pool account
  • Antivirus/DLP quarantine-restore operations rewriting an existing .aspx in place
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("psconfig", "Install-SPSolution", "Add-SPSolution", "stsadm"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Retrieve and read the written file — a short/obfuscated page with eval/Request/Process.Start or MachineKey/web.config access is a web shell; note file SHA256, path, and timestamp, and confirm the May 2026 CVE-2026-45659 patch state. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the server, quarantine/remove the file (retain a copy), kill any live w3wp child process tree, and rotate SharePoint MachineKey/ASP.NET machine keys since forged-request persistence survives file removal. 3) HUNT: Correlate to UC1 (w3wp spawning shells), search IIS logs for POST requests immediately preceding the file write to identify the authenticated account and source IP, and sweep all SharePoint servers for other recently written handlers in LAYOUTS.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FolderPath has @"\TEMPLATE\LAYOUTS\" or FolderPath has @"\Web Server Extensions\"
| where FileName endswith ".aspx" or FileName endswith ".ashx" or FileName endswith ".asmx"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName endswith "w3wp.exe"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\TEMPLATE\LAYOUTS\" or TargetFilePath has @"\Web Server Extensions\"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".aspx" or TargetFileName endswith ".ashx" or TargetFileName endswith ".asmx"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SharePoint w3wp.exe Writing Web Shell to LAYOUTS Directory (CVE-2026-45659 Post-Exploit)
id: 3c9d7e02-1f84-4a6b-b0d5-72e1a9c4f8a3
status: experimental
description: Detects the SharePoint IIS worker (w3wp.exe) creating a web-accessible handler (.aspx/.ashx/.asmx) in the SharePoint LAYOUTS / Web Server Extensions directory, indicative of web-shell drop after CVE-2026-45659 deserialization RCE.
references:

  - https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/sharepoint-vulnerability-rce-active-exploitation-detections-mitigations

      - '.aspx'

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.EXE) @TargetFilename:(*\\TEMPLATE\\LAYOUTS\\*.aspx OR *\\TEMPLATE\\LAYOUTS\\*.ashx OR *\\TEMPLATE\\LAYOUTS\\*.asmx OR *\\Web?Server?Extensions\\*.aspx)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/w3wp\.exe/i
| TargetFileName=/\\(TEMPLATE\\LAYOUTS|Web Server Extensions)\\.*\.(aspx|ashx|asmx)$/i

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="w3wp.exe" AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\TEMPLATE\\LAYOUTS\\*" AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.aspx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ashx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asmx") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="w3wp.exe" AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\TEMPLATE\\LAYOUTS\\*" AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.aspx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ashx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asmx") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45659")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45659")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |

    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase

tags:

    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows

        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'

            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'

    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Web-runtime account creating cron persistence (JADEPUFFER 30-min beacon) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] JADEPUFFER C2 beacon to 45.131.66.106:4444/beacon · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] MinIO factory-default credential use (minioadmin:minioadmin) · [LLM] JADEPUFFER database ransomware artifacts (README_RANSOM, BTC/Proton note, DROP DATABASE) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Langflow unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2025-3248) via /api/v1/validate/code + shell spawn AIExploitation High
Hunts exploitation of the Langflow missing-auth RCE that JADEPUFFER used for initial access: an unauthenticated POST to the code-validation endpoint, and the Langflow Python worker spawning shell/recon children. Article-specific because it anchors on the exact CVE-2025-3248 endpoint and the web-runtime-to-shell lineage rather than generic web exploitation. Rationale: Uses the exact CVE-2025-3248 exploitation endpoint (/api/v1/validate/code, POST) named in the CVE public analysis, and the Langflow-python-worker-spawning-shell lineage from the article's execution phase. Endpoint path is public CVE knowledge, not just this article; C2/recon strings tie it to JADEPUFFER.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow developers legitimately validating custom component code via the UI (internal source IP)
  • Automated CI/CD or health-check probes hitting Langflow API endpoints
  • Security scanners (Nessus/Qualys) POSTing to the validate endpoint during authorized assessments
  • Langflow flow-import operations that legitimately spawn python subprocesses
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("10.", "192.168.", "172.16.") and HttpStatusCode !in ("401","403")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source IP is external/untrusted and that no authenticated session preceded the POST; pull the request body and any child process command lines on the host. 2) Contain: isolate the Langflow host, block the source IP at the perimeter, and rotate every API key / cloud credential stored in the Langflow environment. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host for outbound beacons to 45.131.66.106:4444, new cron entries, and use of minioadmin credentials; verify Langflow is patched to >=1.3.0.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python3","python","uvicorn","gunicorn") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "langflow"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","python3","python")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","/tmp/","uname","whoami","base64","python -c","python3 -c","crontab","minioadmin")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v1/validate/code"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

JADEPUFFER C2 beacon to 45.131.66.106:4444/beacon AICommand & Control Medium
Detects the command-and-control channel from a JADEPUFFER-compromised host: HTTP beacons to 45.131.66.106 on TCP/4444 hitting the /beacon URI on a fixed 30-minute cadence. High-fidelity because it pins the exact published IP, port, and URI. Rationale: Pins the exact Sysdig-published C2 indicator (45.131.66.106, TCP/4444, /beacon) from the command_and_control phase. IP is single-source (Sysdig/THN) so paired with port and URI to raise fidelity; treat a hit as high-confidence given the non-standard port.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1571
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel or sandbox detonation infrastructure deliberately connecting to the C2 for analysis
  • Security researchers on the network validating the IOC
  • Rare re-use of the IP by an unrelated benign service after takedown/reallocation
  • Internal proxy/EDR that resolves the IP during reputation lookups
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process/account on the beaconing host and confirm the 30-minute cadence to /beacon; capture the process tree. 2) Contain: isolate the host and null-route/block 45.131.66.106 at the firewall for all internal ranges. 3) Hunt: search the host for the cron/scheduled-task persistence that drives the beacon, Langflow RCE artifacts, and any pivot to internal MySQL (3306) / Nacos (8848) services.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "45.131.66.106" and RemotePort == 4444
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "45.131.66.106" and DstPortNumber == 4444
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, Url, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Web-runtime account creating cron persistence (JADEPUFFER 30-min beacon) AIInstallation Medium
Detects the persistence step where the AI agent, running under the Langflow/web-service Python runtime, writes a cron entry to re-beacon every 30 minutes. Article-specific because it flags cron artifacts authored by a web-app interpreter rather than by an admin shell or package manager. Rationale: Targets the persistence phase citation ('adding a scheduled task that pinged the attacker's server every 30 minutes') by keying on cron writes whose author is the Langflow/web Python runtime — an abnormal parent for cron on a server. Behavioral, so tiered hunting.
ATT&CKT1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Application deployment scripts written in Python that legitimately install cron jobs
  • Configuration-management agents (Ansible/Salt) invoked via python writing cron.d entries
  • Certbot/letsencrypt renewal hooks writing cron entries
  • A developer using a python virtualenv to register a scheduled maintenance job
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ansible", "salt-minion", "puppet", "certbot", "letsencrypt"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the created cron file's contents and confirm whether it invokes curl/wget/python to an external host (especially 45.131.66.106:4444). 2) Contain: remove the cron entry, isolate the host, and kill the beaconing process. 3) Hunt: correlate to Langflow RCE on the same host, review other cron/systemd units created by the same account, and check for credential-scraping activity that preceded persistence.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/spool/cron", "/etc/cron.d", "/etc/crontab", "/etc/cron.hourly", "/etc/cron.daily")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python3","python","sh","bash","dash","uvicorn","gunicorn","curl","wget") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "langflow"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/spool/cron", "/etc/cron.d", "/etc/crontab", "/etc/cron.hourly", "/etc/cron.daily")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python", "uvicorn", "gunicorn", "sh", "bash", "curl", "wget") or ActingProcessCommandLine has "langflow"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Nacos auth bypass CVE-2021-29441 via User-Agent: Nacos-Server + rogue admin AIExploitation High
Detects the privilege-escalation step where JADEPUFFER abused the Nacos serverIdentity auth bypass — requests to /nacos/v1/auth/users carrying the User-Agent 'Nacos-Server' to enumerate and create an admin account. Article/CVE-specific via the exact endpoint and the header that triggers the bypass. Rationale: Anchors on the public CVE-2021-29441 bypass signature (User-Agent: Nacos-Server against /nacos/v1/auth/users), matching the article's Nacos takeover + planted admin account. Detection lives only on web/proxy telemetry, so Defender/Falcon/Datadog/CloudWatch are left empty — Defender XDR and FDR do not parse inbound Nacos HTTP headers.
ATT&CKT1190 T1136.001 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Nacos cluster nodes communicating with each other (they use the Nacos-Server identity internally, but from known peer IPs)
  • Nacos health-check or sync traffic from trusted intra-cluster addresses
  • Authorized pentest replaying the CVE-2021-29441 PoC
Suppression filter
| where not (SrcIpAddr in ("10.", "192.168.", "172.16."))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source IP is not a legitimate Nacos cluster peer; review whether a new user was created via the response and inspect current Nacos admin accounts. 2) Contain: remove any rogue Nacos admin account, rotate the Nacos signing key off the shipped default, and restrict 8848 to internal peers only. 3) Hunt: trace the source IP back to the Langflow host / C2 45.131.66.106, and check the MySQL backing store for DROP TABLE/DATABASE and a README_RANSOM table.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "/nacos/v1/auth/users"
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has "Nacos-Server"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MinIO factory-default credential use (minioadmin:minioadmin) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the credential-access step where the agent logged into a MinIO server using the never-changed factory default minioadmin:minioadmin. Article-specific through the concrete default-credential string appearing in on-host client command lines (mc / curl / boto). Rationale: Uses the exact default-credential string 'minioadmin' called out in the credential_access phase ('factory-default login minioadmin:minioadmin'). Command-line presence of this string on a production host is a strong default-cred-abuse signal; tiered hunting because legitimate admin/test use exists.
ATT&CKT1078.001 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or admin using minioadmin against a local dev/test MinIO instance that legitimately still uses defaults
  • IaC / container bootstrap scripts that set the initial minioadmin root user before rotation
  • MinIO documentation or tutorial commands run interactively
  • Backup tooling configured with the default alias in a lab environment
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("dev", "test", "lab", "staging"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host, user, and full command line; determine whether the target MinIO endpoint is production and whether the default credential is still active. 2) Contain: rotate/disable the MinIO root credential immediately and restrict the console/API ports from external access. 3) Hunt: check the same host for Langflow RCE, C2 beacons to 45.131.66.106:4444, and whether harvested MinIO-stored secrets were used to pivot to MySQL/Nacos.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "minioadmin"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "minioadmin" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "minioadmin"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

JADEPUFFER database ransomware artifacts (README_RANSOM, BTC/Proton note, DROP DATABASE) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the impact phase: creation of a README_RANSOM table, the ransom note referencing BTC 3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy and e78393397@proton.me, and mass DROP TABLE/DATABASE by a MySQL/root session. Article-specific through the unique ransom-note strings and named artifact table. Rationale: Uses the three unique impact-phase artifacts named in the article: the README_RANSOM table name, the BTC address 3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy, and the Proton contact e78393397@proton.me, plus DROP DATABASE via a MySQL/root session. These strings are effectively zero-FP outside this campaign.
ATT&CKT1486 T1485
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A blue-team / DFIR analyst grepping logs or a threat-intel feed that contains these IOC strings on a monitored host
  • IOC-scanning tooling that echoes the BTC/email strings while searching
  • Documentation or this very advisory opened in a shell/editor with the strings in the command
  • Legitimate DROP DATABASE during an authorized DBA migration (only matched via the has_all fallback)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("grep","rg","less","cat","vim","nano") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("grep","rg "))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the process context is a genuine DB session (mysql/mysqld) and not an analyst grepping IOCs; check the target DB for a README_RANSOM table and dropped schemas. 2) Contain: isolate the DB host, revoke external access to the MySQL root account, and snapshot the volume for forensics before any recovery attempt. 3) Hunt: trace the intrusion chain back through Nacos (CVE-2021-29441), the C2 45.131.66.106:4444, and the Langflow RCE origin; note per Sysdig the encryption key was never saved, so prioritize backups over ransom payment.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("README_RANSOM", "3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy", "e78393397@proton.me")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("DROP", "DATABASE") and FileName in~ ("mysql","mysqld","sh","bash"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (Syslog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where SyslogMessage has_any ("README_RANSOM","3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy","e78393397@proton.me") | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, EvidenceCol=SyslogMessage),
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("README_RANSOM","3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy","e78393397@proton.me") | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ProcessName=ActingProcessName, EvidenceCol=ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| regex("(README_RANSOM|3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy|e78393397@proton\.me)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*README_RANSOM*" OR Processes.process="*3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy*" OR Processes.process="*e78393397@proton.me*") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*README_RANSOM*" OR Processes.process="*3J98t1WpEZ73CNmQviecrnyiWrnqRhWNLy*" OR Processes.process="*e78393397@proton.me*") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| sort - count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-3248", "CVE-2021-29441")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-3248", "CVE-2021-29441")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-3248", "CVE-2021-29441")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-3248", "CVE-2021-29441")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
